title: Organic Traffic vs. Paid Traffic for Affiliates | Digistore24 Blog

facts.fact: The page states that paid traffic requires a minimum of $500–$1,000 per month to test properly.
facts.quote: Paid traffic requires real money to test properly — at minimum $500–$1,000/month.

facts.fact: The page states that organic traffic takes 3–6 months to generate meaningful volume.
facts.quote: Organic traffic takes 3–6 months before it generates meaningful volume.

facts.fact: The page states that organic search still drives 53% of all website traffic, without citing a source in the text.
facts.quote: still drives 53% of all website traffic

facts.fact: The page states that organic visitors convert at 2–3% on average, compared with 1–2% for paid traffic, without citing a source in the text.
facts.quote: organic visitors convert at 2–3% on average, compared to 1–2% for paid traffic

facts.fact: The page defines ROAS for affiliate paid traffic as commissions earned divided by ad spend.
The page states that a ROAS above 1 means an affiliate campaign is profitable, and that most affiliates target a ROAS of 2:1 or 3:1 before scaling.
facts.quote: Most affiliates target 2:1 or 3:1 before scaling.

facts.fact: The page states that average cost-per-click across major ad platforms rose roughly 18% in 2025, without citing a source in the text.
facts.quote: Average cost-per-click across major ad platforms rose roughly 18% in 2025.

facts.fact: The page's comparison table lists 24–72 hours as the time to first results for paid traffic, versus 3–6 months for organic.
facts.quote: Time to first results | 3–6 months | 24–72 hours

facts.fact: The article is dated September 21, 2026 and written by Luke Sheehan.
The page lists Facebook Ads, Google Ads, YouTube Ads, TikTok Ads, and native advertising networks as examples of paid traffic sources.
facts.quote: through Facebook Ads, Google Ads, YouTube Ads, TikTok Ads, or native advertising networks.
